source.work: Domain-Driven Design (E. Evans, 2003); Implementing Domain-Driven Design (V. Vernon, 2013)
source.locator: Evans ch. 5, Value Objects; Vernon ch. 6, Value Objects
source.paraphrase: A value object is defined only by its attributes and treated as immutable: to change a value, replace it with a new one instead of altering it in place.

invariants.why: A shared value that changes in place changes every holder at once, breaking equality by value and the rules checked at construction.
invariants.fixHint: Make every field readonly and return a new instance from each operation that would change the value.
invariants.avoid: Private mutable fields behind getters, public constructor parameter properties, and writes through Object.assign or casts.

relations.why: Under value-object paths DDD-ENT-002 also reports a public mutable field, which DDD-VO-001 already reports as a field that is not readonly.
relations.settle: Keep both: the repair (a readonly or private field) satisfies each. To report it once, add the value-object globs to exclude on DDD-ENT-002.

source.work: Domain-Driven Design (E. Evans, 2003); Implementing Domain-Driven Design (V. Vernon, 2013)
source.locator: Evans ch. 5, Entities; Vernon ch. 5, Entities
source.paraphrase: An entity keeps its identity and guards its own consistency: its state changes through operations that express domain intent, not through raw writes to its properties.

invariants.why: A public setter lets any caller put the entity into a state its own rules never allowed.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the setter with a method named after the domain operation, which checks the entity's rules before changing state; take the name from the glossary or the domain.
invariants.avoid: Renaming the setter, computing its name, returning this from it, or exposing it as an arrow-function property.

source.work: Domain-Driven Design (E. Evans, 2003); Implementing Domain-Driven Design (V. Vernon, 2013)
source.locator: Evans ch. 5, Entities; Vernon ch. 5, Entities
source.paraphrase: An entity keeps its identity and guards its own consistency: its state changes through operations that express domain intent, not through raw writes to its properties.

invariants.why: A public field that is not readonly is a setter with no body: any caller can write order.status = "paid" and skip every rule the entity checks.
invariants.fixHint: Make the field private (or readonly if it never changes), expose a getter if callers need to read it, and change it only inside a method named after the domain operation.
invariants.avoid: Static fields, function-valued fields and fields outside the configured paths are not checked. Persistence-mapped classes kept under domain/ are reported too; map them to the domain type in the adapter instead of loosening the entity.

relations.why: Under value-object paths DDD-VO-001 already reports every field that is not readonly, so a public mutable field there is reported by both rules.
relations.settle: Keep both: the repair (a readonly or private field) satisfies each. To report it once, add the value-object globs to exclude on DDD-ENT-002.

relations.why: A public constructor parameter property is reported by DDD-ENT-002 as mutable state and by TS-LEGACY-005 as a parameter property.
relations.settle: Declare a private field and assign it in the constructor body; that satisfies both rules.
